Subject: [URGENT] Edge escape: US/EU/APAC diversion & customer cutover checklist

Hi all —

We wanted to notify you immediately that a third-party peering disruption affecting multiple cloud regions (US-West, EU-Central, APAC-East) has resulted in elevated token latency and partial request failures for customers routing through the affected fabric. Our on-call engineering team is actively mitigating; we expect automatic routing to continue to shift traffic over the next 30–60 minutes.

Immediate customer-facing guidance (what you should do now):
- If you can tolerate slightly higher latency for a short window, no action required — our smart routing will continue to attempt automated fallback.
- If you need deterministic regional failover, switch calls to the alternate regional endpoints below (short-term):
  • US: https://api.redwood.dev?region=us-east-1 (preferred) or set header X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
  • EU: https://eu.api.redwood.dev?region=eu-west-1 or header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
  • APAC: https://apac.api.redwood.dev?region=apac-sg-1 or header X-Redwood-Region: apac-sg-1
- For SDK users, upgrade to client 1.7.3 (hotfix) which includes a regional preference flag (client.regionalFallback = true) to reduce 5xx surface area.

Attachments: edge-escape-checklist.pdf (one-page quick steps), region-diversion-map.png

We've opened SUP-98234 and posted live updates to the status page: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/2026-06-20-edge-escape

We'll send a second update with timelines and any required customer cutover checklists in ~30 minutes. Sorry for the disruption — reaching out directly to orgs with active sessions now.

— Jasmine

Daniel —
Short answer: yes. The alternate regional endpoints are fully compatible with existing org/tenant authentication tokens; there is no re-auth required for JWT-based tokens issued within the last 24 hours. A couple notes:
- If you use long-lived sessions (>24h), please rotate tokens after cutover to be safe.
- The us-east-1 region will honor tenant routing headers (X-Org-ID, X-Redwood-Env). If you want client-side deterministic cutover, set header X-Redwood-Force-Region: us-east-1 for the call during the window.

We will watch latency and open a dedicated bridge if you want an engineer on the call during your run.

Subject: Incident wrap & next steps — postmortem draft and customer check-ins

Hi everyone — thank you for your patience and for the quick cooperation from your ops teams. Summary and next steps: 

What happened
- 06:50 PDT: a downstream cloud peering fabric experienced route flaps that caused partial packet loss between our edge POPs and a subset of cloud egress nodes in US-West, EU-Central, and APAC-East.
- 07:05 PDT: Redwood automatic fallback (reserve fabric + cross-region spill) engaged.
- 07:25–09:00 PDT: customer impact peaked (increased token latency and occasional 5xx).
- 09:05 PDT: error rate returned below 0.5% for affected customers after progressive traffic shift and BGP convergence.

Customer guidance recap (attached checklist)
- Use the provided alternate endpoints or set X-Redwood-Force-Region if you need deterministic routing.
- SDK hotfix v1.7.3 contains automatic regional fallback — clients should be upgraded within the week if you have long-running sessions.
- If you require a guaranteed tenant-preserving cutover window, please reply to this thread with preferred times and your org ID; we will coordinate a staffed migration.

Follow-ups we are taking
- Internal postmortem (SUP-98234) — draft attached. We will publish a customer-friendly postmortem by Tue, 2026-06-22 17:00 UTC.
- Engineering action items include BGP session hardening, additional reserve fabric capacity, and expanded health-probing to detect peering flaps earlier.
- Sales/CS: outreach to impacted accounts for any SLA or credit remediation requests.

If you'd like a live debrief or an on-call engineer during your next run, tell us a time and we will arrange it. Apologies again for the disruption — we know these windows are painful and appreciate the partnership.

Best —
